text:
Agent: Thank you for calling BrightLine Broadband, this is Kayla. How can I help you today?
Customer: Hi Kayla. Yeah, my internet's been down since about six this morning. The router's got a red light on it, and I've already unplugged it twice.
Agent: I'm sorry to hear that. Can I get the account holder's name and the postcode on the account?
Customer: It's Daniel Mercer, postcode is, um, M-four-two, nine-F-R.
Agent: Thanks Daniel. Let me pull up your line. Okay, I can see there's a reported fault in your area, a cable cut near Oakfield Road. Engineers are on site.
Customer: Oh, so it's not just me. Any idea when it'll be back? I work from home and I've got a call at one.
Agent: The estimate on my screen says it should be restored by two this afternoon, but those are never exact. Do you have a mobile phone you can tether to?
Customer: I do, but my data plan is only five gigs.
Agent: I can add a free data boost to your mobile if you're with us for that as well. Are you?
Customer: No, the mobile's with another provider.
Agent: Understood. In that case I'd suggest the free public hotspot, you may have a BrightLine hotspot nearby at the library. Otherwise, we do give an automatic credit for outages longer than twenty-four hours.
Customer: This will be under twenty-four, so no credit?
Agent: That's right, I'm afraid. But let me note on your account that you've called, and I'll send you a text update the moment the engineers mark it fixed.
Customer: Okay. That's something. And if it's not fixed by two, do I need to call again?
Agent: No need. If it's still down by four, the system escalates automatically and a supervisor will phone you.
Customer: Alright, thanks Kayla.
Agent: You're welcome, Daniel. Sorry again for the trouble. Have a good day.
